title: Offline world data for The Mathematics of You
recordSchema: Each observation inherits its unit, source, access date and notes from the containing series unless the observation supplies a more specific source URL or note.

methodology.latestYearRule: Use the last non-null published observation in each series. Never label that value as today when its data year is earlier.
methodology.birthYearRule: Use an official observation for the visitor's birth year when one exists. Do not silently substitute the closest year.
methodology.interpolationFormula: estimated value = y0 + ((date - date0) / (date1 - date0)) * (y1 - y0)
methodology.interpolationRule: Interpolate only between adjacent observations when the series explicitly allows it, label the result as interpolated, and name both surrounding years. No extrapolation is allowed.
methodology.purchasingPowerFormula: equivalent rupees in latest data year = rupees in birth year * (latest CPI / birth-year CPI)
methodology.marketGrowthFormula: price-index growth (%) = ((latest year-end close / birth-year year-end close) - 1) * 100

indiaPopulation.label: Population, total — India

interpolation.reason: Population is a continuously changing stock; linear interpolation between adjacent annual mid-year estimates is a transparent approximation for an in-year date.

source.title: World Bank Open Data — Population, total (India)
source.underlyingProvider: United Nations Population Division, national statistical offices and other sources listed by World Bank

notes: These are data-based annual population estimates, not an exact head count.
World Bank describes total population as a mid-year estimate; the UI should format counts without implying census-level precision.

worldPopulation.label: Population, total — World

interpolation.reason: Population is a continuously changing stock; linear interpolation between adjacent annual mid-year estimates is a transparent approximation for an in-year date.

source.title: World Bank Open Data — Population, total (World)
source.underlyingProvider: United Nations Population Division, national statistical offices and other sources listed by World Bank

notes: These are data-based annual population estimates, not an exact head count.
The World aggregate is the value returned for World Bank economy code WLD.

indiaInternetUse.label: Individuals using the Internet — India

interpolation.reason: The annual values combine survey and administrative evidence; adoption is not assumed to change uniformly within or across years.

source.title: World Bank Open Data — Individuals using the Internet (% of population), India
source.underlyingProvider: International Telecommunication Union, World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database

notes: This indicator estimates the share of people who used the Internet from any location during the reference period.
Show the published data year and round only for display; retain the stored values for calculation.

indiaElectricityAccess.label: Access to electricity — India

interpolation.reason: Use the official annual estimates; electrification programmes and estimation revisions make straight-line in-year change a poor default assumption.

source.title: World Bank Open Data — Access to electricity (% of population), India

notes: Access means having an electricity source that can provide basic energy services; this is an estimated population share.
The latest available API observation is 2024, not 2026.

atmosphericCo2MaunaLoa.label: Atmospheric carbon dioxide — Mauna Loa annual mean
atmosphericCo2MaunaLoa.geography: Mauna Loa Observatory, Hawaii (with the documented 2022–2023 site interruption)

interpolation.reason: The website compares published annual means; a birth-date concentration would require the separate monthly series and seasonal adjustment.

source.title: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory — Mauna Loa CO₂ annual mean data
source.provider: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory; Xin Lan and Ralph Keeling

notes: CO₂ is expressed as micromoles per mole of dry air, abbreviated ppm.
NOAA says the uncertainty column is estimated from independently determined NOAA and Scripps annual means; values may receive small quality-control revisions.

Mauna Loa observations were suspended after 29 November 2022 and resumed in July 2023; observations from December 2022 to 4 July 2023 came from Maunakea Observatories, as documented in the source file.

indiaConsumerPriceIndex.label: Consumer price index — India

derivedCalculation.name: ₹100 birth-year purchasing-power equivalent
derivedCalculation.assumption: A broad national CPI basket is used as an educational purchasing-power comparison; an individual household's spending pattern can differ substantially.

interpolation.reason: The entries are annual-average indices. Use the visitor's calendar-year observation rather than manufacturing a daily CPI.

source.title: World Bank Open Data — Consumer price index (2010 = 100), India
source.underlyingProvider: International Monetary Fund, International Financial Statistics database

notes: The index ratio, not the base-year label, drives the ₹100 equivalence.
The result is a broad inflation adjustment and must not be described as an exact price for any particular item.
An RBI/NSO fiscal-year CPI Combined series is also stored below for Indian-source context, but it is not mixed with this calendar-year series.

indiaConsumerPriceInflation.label: Inflation, consumer prices — India

interpolation.reason: Inflation is itself a change over a defined annual interval; interpolation between annual rates would not preserve the underlying price-index path.

source.title: World Bank Open Data — Inflation, consumer prices (annual %), India
source.underlyingProvider: International Monetary Fund, International Financial Statistics database

notes: This is the annual percentage change in the consumer price index; it is not cumulative inflation since birth.
Use the CPI-index ratio above for the ₹100 equivalence.

indiaLifeExpectancy.label: Life expectancy at birth, total — India

interpolation.reason: Use published annual demographic estimates; shocks and model revisions mean the series should not be treated as locally linear by default.

source.title: World Bank Open Data — Life expectancy at birth, total (years), India
source.underlyingProvider: United Nations Population Division and national statistical sources listed by World Bank

notes: Life expectancy at birth is a period population statistic, not a prediction of the visitor's lifespan.
The COVID-era fall and subsequent rebound are present in the published series and should not be smoothed away.
The latest available observation is 2024.

indiaAdultLiteracy.label: Literacy rate, adult total — India
indiaAdultLiteracy.displayPolicy: Compare only when the visitor's birth year has a stored official observation. Otherwise omit the comparison and explain that no comparable birth-year observation is bundled.

interpolation.reason: Observations are sparse and can reflect different surveys or estimation rounds; straight-line interpolation would imply unsupported precision.

source.title: World Bank Open Data — Literacy rate, adult total (% ages 15+), India
source.underlyingProvider: UNESCO Institute for Statistics Data API

notes: Do not present this sparse series as a smooth yearly trend.
The 2023 and 2024 observations differ sharply; that is another reason to show source years and avoid interpolation.
For a 2011 birth year, both 2011 and the latest year have official observations.

indiaCpiCombinedFiscalRbi.label: All-India CPI Combined annual average — RBI/NSO fiscal-year series

interpolation.reason: The observations are fiscal-year averages; do not interpolate or combine them with the calendar-year World Bank/IMF CPI series.

source.title: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy — Table 37: Consumer Price Index, Annual Average
source.underlyingProvider: National Statistical Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India

notes: CPI Combined covers rural plus urban India and was introduced from January 2011; the series uses base 2012 = 100.
This official Indian fiscal-year series is retained for source transparency and cross-checking. The website's birth-calendar-year ₹100 comparison uses the separate calendar-year CPI series above.
The cited RBI table's latest complete fiscal-year observation is 2023-24.

nifty50YearEnd.label: NIFTY 50 price index — year-end close
nifty50YearEnd.frequency: last available official December close for each calendar year

derivedCalculation.name: NIFTY 50 price-index growth
derivedCalculation.formula: growth (%) = ((latest year-end close / birth-year year-end close) - 1) * 100
derivedCalculation.assumption: This compares year-end price-index levels. It excludes dividends, fees, taxes and the exact timing of a visitor's birth, so it is not an investment-return calculation.

interpolation.reason: Market prices are not linearly interpolated. Use only the stored official closing observations.

source.title: National Stock Exchange of India — Historical Index Data
source.archivePattern: NSE archives filename pattern: ind_close_all_DDMMYYYY.csv (substitute the requested date)

notes: NIFTY 50 was named S&P CNX Nifty in 2012, CNX Nifty in 2013–2014, and Nifty 50 in later archive files; these observations refer to the same benchmark lineage.
The 2011 point is the 30 December final-trading-day close shown through NSE's official historical-index data service; the later static daily archive pattern was not available for that date.
Do not describe this price-index change as money earned: it excludes dividends and all investor-specific costs.

values.note: Final trading-day close for calendar year 2011; verified through NSE's official historical-index data service.

genuineLimitations: The compact offline bundle begins in 2011. A visitor born earlier needs an expanded historical file or a clearly stated unavailable comparison; the UI must not reuse 2011 as though it were their birth-year value.
Different series end in different years. The interface must print each series' actual latest year.
World Bank values can be revised after this access date. The saved observations intentionally remain frozen so the exhibition continues to work offline and reproducibly.
Adult-literacy observations are irregular and must not be interpolated.
The NIFTY series is a price-index comparison at annual endpoints, not a personalised investment return.
